extracted.intended_audience: journal editors, society publishers, scholarly communications professionals, researchers interested in peer review equity
extracted.subtask_short: reducing gender bias in peer review
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance and empirical criteria for detecting, monitoring, and reducing gender (and other demographic) bias in journal peer review processes, with emphasis on data collection, analysis, and simple interventions (author/editor instructions, experiments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare reviewer gender representation to expected distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure whether women are used as reviewers at rates lower than expected based on membership distribution or author profile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine membership and editorial data to calculate expected proportions; examine reviewer usage versus expectation within age cohorts and author profiles; use this to identify underrepresentation (the AGU finding: 'women were less likely to be used as reviewers, compared to what one would expect based on the membership distribution or author profile').

rubrics_metrics.name: Collect demographic data in editorial and membership systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Have reliable self-reported data on gender, age, and ethnicity available in editorial systems so bias can be evaluated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a society publisher, AGU combined membership self-reported data with editorial records. Improve data collection going forward (expand categories, increase participation) because incomplete ethnic data limits ability to detect effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for age cohorts when evaluating bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Use age data to control for historical underrepresentation (e.g., fewer women in older cohorts) when assessing reviewer and author gender patterns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because women are much more represented in younger cohorts (AGU example: nearly 50% women under 30 but <10% over 70), comparisons must be age-adjusted to avoid misleading conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor source of reviewer suggestions (authors vs editors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Track how much the reviewer pool comes from author suggestions versus editor-solicited reviewers and the gender composition of each source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors' suggestions are typically used about 30% of the time; editors suggest the other reviewers. Compare gender breakdowns separately for author-suggested and editor-suggested reviewers to identify where bias enters (AGU found authors suggested fewer women).

rubrics_metrics.name: Add explicit diversity reminder to author instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Ask authors, via the submission instructions, to consider diversity (gender, age, ethnic, international) when suggesting reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AGU added this statement: 'Please help us improve the diversity of our reviewer pool by including women, young scientists, and members of other underrepresented groups in your suggested reviewers (e.g., age, ethnic, and international diversity).' A pre/post comparison (three months before/after) showed a significant increase in suggested women reviewers, especially from male authors (+4%).

rubrics_metrics.name: Include diversity reminder in editor reviewer recommendation step
rubrics_metrics.description: Prompt editors, when they recommend reviewers, to consider diversity, since editors' suggestions also shape the reviewer pool.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AGU found editors suggest more women than authors, and women editors do better than male editors, but still below expectation—so adding the same reminder for editors can help.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track invitation and decline rates by demographic groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure both invitation rates and decline rates for reviewers broken down by gender and age to identify differential willingness/availability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AGU observed a 'slightly higher decline rate among women in each age group when asked'—tracking declines helps distinguish selection bias from response patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyze co-authorship and reviewer-recommendation networks for homophily
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine authors' co-author networks and recommender patterns to detect homophily (tendency to interact with same-gender colleagues) that can perpetuate bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AGU found men tend to have predominantly male co-authors while women author networks are more balanced; this network structure likely influences reviewer suggestions and selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use controlled pre/post experiments to test interventions
rubrics_metrics.description: When implementing policy changes (e.g., adding instructions), compare relevant metrics before and after the change to assess impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AGU compared a three-month period before and after adding the diversity statement at Geophysical Research Letters and used statistical tests (reported χ²) to quantify change in suggested women reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure reviewer pool geographic diversity relative to submission origins
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare the geographic composition of the reviewer pool to the geographic distribution of accepted/submitted papers and take steps to fill gaps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AGU noted reviewer pool was dominated by U.S./Europe while ~30% of accepted submissions were from Asia—efforts should be made to expand reviewer participation from underrepresented regions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improve and expand demographic categories and participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Refine demographic categories (especially for ethnicity) and encourage member/researcher participation in providing this data to get meaningful analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AGU's ethnic data were incomplete and categories limited; improving data quality and completeness is critical to detect ethnic or other biases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor bias in related scholarly activities (meetings, invited speakers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Extend bias monitoring beyond peer review to other selection processes such as invited speakers, poster vs oral selections, and conference programming.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AGU plans to look at annual meeting selections and invited speaker lists for bias, indicating that peer-review bias may be one of multiple manifestations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leverage editors' demographics as an explanatory variable
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider editors' gender (and other demographics) when analyzing reviewer selection patterns, since editor characteristics influence reviewer suggestions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AGU found women editors suggest more women reviewers than male editors, suggesting editorial demographics shape reviewer diversity and can be a lever for change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborate across societies/publishers to pool data and best practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Small publishers with limited data should collaborate with other organizations to create a larger dataset for detecting and addressing bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AGU suggests society publishers work together because single-society datasets may be too small; pooled data enable more robust measurement and coordinated interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report findings and solicit community participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Share analyses and invite the community to contribute demographic data and suggestions to improve diversity-monitoring efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AGU emphasizes active participation from members to provide demographic data, and the interview itself and linked posts serve as public reporting and invitation for feedback.
